_about: Curated seed knowledge base. Descriptions are the project's own words; facts are limited to names, cities, categories and official websites. Opening times and prices change, so the app always tells users to check the official website. Verify every entry before a public release (scripts/check_links.py checks the links).

places.name: Zoo Berlin
places.description: Germany's oldest zoo, opened in 1844, right in the city centre near Berlin Zoologischer Garten station. Families can spend a full day here, and several animal houses keep it worthwhile on cooler days.

places.name: Tierpark Berlin
places.description: A very large landscape zoo in Friedrichsfelde in eastern Berlin with wide paths through park land. Good for long walks with a pram and for children who like to run between enclosures.

places.name: Deutsches Technikmuseum
places.description: A large technology museum in Kreuzberg with historic locomotives, aircraft and ships. Its hands-on science centre lets children try experiments themselves, which makes it a strong rainy-day choice.

places.name: Museum für Naturkunde
places.description: Berlin's natural history museum, best known for its hall of towering dinosaur skeletons. Children who love dinosaurs, minerals and animals can explore it in two to three hours.

places.name: Labyrinth Kindermuseum Berlin
places.description: A children's museum in Wedding built around playful, hands-on exhibitions where children climb, build and discover. Made for preschool and primary school ages.

places.name: LEGOLAND Discovery Centre Berlin
places.description: An indoor LEGO play centre at Potsdamer Platz with building areas, small rides and a 4D cinema. A compact outing of a few hours for younger LEGO fans.

places.name: Deutsches Museum
places.description: One of the world's largest museums of science and technology, on an island in the Isar river. Part of the building is closed for modernisation until about 2028, including the mine; aviation, space travel, robotics and the Kinderreich for younger children are open, so check the website for what is open before you go.

places.name: Tierpark Hellabrunn
places.description: Munich's zoo on the banks of the Isar, laid out by continents so animals live in regional groups. It has a children's zoo where little ones can get close to farm animals.

places.name: LEGOLAND Deutschland Resort
places.description: A LEGO theme park in Bavaria with rides, shows and Miniland models built from millions of bricks. It opens seasonally, so check the calendar before planning a day trip.

places.name: Miniatur Wunderland
places.description: The world's largest model railway, in a warehouse in Hamburg's Speicherstadt, with tiny landscapes, airports and cities that switch between day and night. Booking a time slot ahead helps avoid queues.

places.name: Tierpark Hagenbeck
places.description: A family-founded zoo known for pioneering open enclosures without bars, plus a tropical aquarium on site that needs its own ticket. The mix of outdoor zoo and indoor aquarium suits changeable weather.

places.name: Senckenberg Naturmuseum Frankfurt
places.description: One of Germany's largest natural history museums, with a famous collection of dinosaur skeletons and fossils. A classic rainy-day outing for curious children.

places.name: Zoo Frankfurt
places.description: A city-centre zoo in Frankfurt's east end with an animal house for nocturnal animals, where day and night are reversed. Compact enough for a half-day visit with small children.

places.name: Kölner Zoo
places.description: Cologne's zoo, with a large elephant park and an aquarium building. A full-day outing next to the Rhine and the city's cable car.

places.name: Schokoladenmuseum Köln
places.description: A chocolate museum on the Rhine harbour that shows how chocolate is made, from cocoa beans to finished bars. Children usually love the tasting at the chocolate fountain.

places.name: Natural History Museum
places.description: A free national museum in South Kensington, famous for its dinosaur gallery and the blue whale skeleton in its grand main hall. Arrive early at weekends and in school holidays.

places.name: Science Museum
places.description: A free museum next to the Natural History Museum with spacecraft, engines and medical history. Its interactive gallery is ticketed but very popular with children who like experiments.

places.name: ZSL London Zoo
places.description: One of the world's oldest scientific zoos, in Regent's Park, run by a conservation charity. Walk-through exhibits and indoor animal houses make it a full-day trip.

places.name: Young V&A
places.description: A free museum in Bethnal Green designed for children and young people, with play, design and imagination galleries. Works well for babies and toddlers as well as school-age children.

places.name: Diana Memorial Playground
places.description: A free playground in Kensington Gardens, renewed in 2026 around a large pirate ship on a sandy beach, with sand and water play (the water play can be switched off in dry spells). Adults may only enter with a child, which keeps it focused on families.

places.name: SEA LIFE London Aquarium
places.description: An aquarium on the South Bank near the London Eye, with sharks, penguins and rays. An easy indoor visit to combine with a walk along the Thames.

places.name: LEGOLAND Windsor Resort
places.description: A LEGO theme park west of London with rides and models aimed at children up to about twelve. It opens seasonally and books up in school holidays.

places.name: Science and Industry Museum
places.description: A free museum on the site of the world's oldest surviving passenger railway station, telling the story of Manchester's industry and science. Parts of the site, including the 1830 Station and Warehouse, are closed during a long restoration, but the Power Hall and the hands-on Experiment gallery are open.

places.name: LEGOLAND Discovery Centre Manchester
places.description: An indoor LEGO attraction at the Trafford Centre with building zones, small rides and a 4D cinema. Good for a few hours with younger children on a wet day.

places.name: National Museum of Scotland
places.description: A free museum in Edinburgh's Old Town covering nature, science, world cultures and Scottish history. Its interactive galleries and rooftop views make it a family favourite.

places.name: Edinburgh Zoo
places.description: A hillside zoo run by a wildlife conservation charity, west of the city centre. Its penguins and daily animal talks are popular with younger visitors; wear good shoes for the slopes.

places.name: Dynamic Earth
places.description: An Earth science centre at the foot of Arthur's Seat that takes visitors through volcanoes, ice and rainforest. A good indoor plan when Edinburgh weather turns wet.

places.name: We The Curious
places.description: A hands-on science centre on Bristol's harbourside with a planetarium. Exhibits invite children to ask questions and test ideas themselves; children under 6 cannot watch the 3D planetarium shows.

places.name: Bristol Zoo Project
places.description: A conservation zoo on the northern edge of Bristol with large, natural-looking habitats and woodland. Plan for lots of walking outdoors.

places.name: Thinktank Birmingham Science Museum
places.description: A science museum at Millennium Point with interactive galleries and a planetarium. Its hands-on galleries suit primary school children especially well.

places.name: Cadbury World
places.description: A chocolate-themed attraction in Bournville, home of Cadbury, mixing the brand's history with interactive zones. Tickets are booked for a set time.

places.name: American Museum of Natural History
places.description: A giant natural history museum on the Upper West Side with dinosaur halls, a life-size blue whale model and a planetarium. Pick two or three halls rather than trying to see it all.

places.name: Bronx Zoo
places.description: One of the largest city zoos in the United States, run by a wildlife conservation society. It is big, so plan a route and expect plenty of walking.

places.name: Children's Museum of Manhattan
places.description: A children's museum on the Upper West Side designed for babies up to six-year-olds, with play-based exhibits. A calm indoor option for toddlers in a busy city.

places.name: New York Hall of Science
places.description: A hands-on science centre in Flushing Meadows Corona Park, Queens, with hundreds of interactive exhibits. Great for children who learn by doing.

places.name: Central Park
places.description: Manhattan's huge park with many playgrounds, a carousel, lawns and boating. Free to enter and easy to combine with nearby museums.

places.name: Exploratorium
places.description: A famous hands-on science museum on Pier 15 by the Bay, full of experiments about light, sound and perception. Curious children can easily spend a whole day.

places.name: California Academy of Sciences
places.description: A museum in Golden Gate Park that combines an aquarium, a planetarium, a rainforest dome and a natural history museum under one living roof. Many families make it a full-day visit.

places.name: San Francisco Zoo
places.description: A zoo near Ocean Beach in the southwest of the city, with a children's zoo area for younger visitors. Bring a layer: it is often foggy and cool by the ocean.

places.name: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
places.description: One of the largest science museums in the Americas (formerly the Museum of Science and Industry), in Hyde Park, with a real German submarine from the Second World War and a huge model railroad. Plenty of hands-on exhibits for school-age children.

places.name: Shedd Aquarium
places.description: A large aquarium on Chicago's lakefront Museum Campus with marine mammals, reefs and freshwater exhibits. Easy to pair with the Field Museum next door.

places.name: Field Museum
places.description: A natural history museum on the Museum Campus, home of SUE, one of the most complete T. rex skeletons ever found. A must for dinosaur fans.

places.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
places.description: A free zoo in Lincoln Park on the North Side, small enough to see in a morning with toddlers. Its farm area lets young children meet familiar animals.

places.name: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
places.description: A free Smithsonian museum on the National Mall with historic aircraft and spacecraft. Check the website for free timed-entry passes before you go.

places.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
places.description: A free museum on the National Mall with a fossil hall, an ocean hall and a famous gem collection. A great first stop for families visiting Washington.

places.name: Smithsonian's National Zoo
places.description: A free zoo in Rock Creek Park run by the Smithsonian. The paths are hilly, so a carrier or sturdy stroller helps with small children; check the website for entry passes.

places.name: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County
places.description: A natural history museum in Exposition Park with a dinosaur hall and outdoor nature gardens. Pairs well with the science centre next door.

places.name: California Science Center
places.description: A science centre in Exposition Park with free general admission. The Space Shuttle Endeavour stands upright in its new Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center, which needs a timed reservation with a small fee; some special exhibits and shows are ticketed too.

places.name: Griffith Observatory
places.description: A hilltop observatory in Griffith Park with free entry to its building and grounds and views over Los Angeles. Planetarium shows are ticketed; parking fills up early.
